terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.intro: These terms (and end-user licence agreement, EULA) apply between you and {controller} for your use of Speak, in the iOS app and on the website. By signing up or using the service you accept them. If you do not agree, do not use Speak.

sections.heading: The service
body: Speak is a voice social network: you post short voices (up to 2 minutes) with an optional title in sections and topics, listen, reply with your voice, like and repost, follow other people and send listen-once voice messages to people you follow mutually.
The service is free and provided "as is" and "as available". We may change, add or remove features or discontinue the service, letting you know where reasonable.

sections.heading: Your account
body: You must be at least 15 years old. Give accurate details, keep one account per person and do not impersonate another person or organisation.
Keep your password safe; you are responsible for activity on your account. If you suspect unauthorised access, change your password and tell us at {email}.

sections.heading: Your content
body: The voices, titles and messages you create belong to you. You give us a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free licence to store, reproduce and distribute them within the service, only to run it. The licence ends when you delete the content or your account.
Your public voices can be heard by every Speak user, who may reply, like, repost or quote them with their own voice. Do not post anything you would not want heard publicly.
You are responsible for having the rights to what you post: do not record or post other people's voices without their consent and do not use music or third-party material without permission.

sections.heading: Zero tolerance for objectionable content and abusive users
body: Speak has zero tolerance for objectionable content and abusive behaviour. In particular, the following are not allowed:

• hate speech or discrimination based on origin, religion, gender, sexual orientation, disability or any other characteristic; • harassment, bullying, threats or targeting people; • sexual content, and any content that sexualises minors; • violence, incitement to violence or encouraging self-harm; • illegal content or promoting illegal activities; • spam, scams, misleading advertising or mass automated actions; • sharing other people's personal details (address, phone number, etc.); • false information that can cause real harm; • copyright infringement; • attempts to bypass security measures or blocks.
If you break these rules we remove the content and may suspend or permanently close your account, without notice for serious or repeated violations.

sections.heading: Reporting, blocking and moderation
body: Every voice, profile, conversation and person on the map has "Report" and "Block". When you block someone, neither of you sees the other's content and you cannot contact each other.

We review every report within 24 hours and remove the content, or ban the user who posted it, when it breaks these terms. A voice reported by several people is hidden automatically until it is reviewed.

We do not review content before it is posted and are not responsible for what users say, but we act promptly once we become aware of illegal or prohibited content. For urgent matters write to {email}.

sections.heading: Student campus
body: Only people who confirm with their university email that they belong to a university can enter its campus. One university email matches one account; using someone else's email or selling/handing over an account is forbidden.
Campus voices, school and year groups and campus topics are for its students only. Don't repost them outside the campus and don't record or share other people's voices without their consent.

Bullying, harassment and publishing personal details of fellow students, teaching staff or employees are forbidden, as is sharing exam questions or answers during an exam and material that infringes copyright.
Student moderators, appointed by Speak, see the reports on their campus's voices (without seeing who made them) and can hide them; decisions about accounts are taken by Speak.
With an invite link, the new user and the person who invited them start following each other; either can change that at any time.

sections.heading: Course notes and past papers
body: On each course page the university's students upload notes and past exam papers (PDF or photos, up to 20 MB). The files, with your name, are visible only to verified students of the same university.

Upload only what you have the right to share: your own notes, exam papers, or material the teaching staff have made freely available. Do not upload textbooks, books, paid or protected third-party material, or other people's personal data (e.g. names and grades).
Every file has “Report” (including copyright). A file reported by three different people is hidden until we review it; we remove infringing files when the rights holder tells us at {email}.

sections.heading: Map and talking to people nearby
body: Sharing your location is optional and you can turn it off at any time. With “Everyone nearby” strangers within 500 m see your exact position — only turn it on if you really want that.

You may not use the map to follow, track or harass anyone, to keep talking to someone who showed they don't want it, or to share another person's location. Be careful if you meet in person someone you met here.
Every person's card on the map has “Report” and “Block”; someone you block no longer sees you or talks to you. Abuse leads to a ban. In danger, call 112.

sections.heading: Listen-once voice messages
body: Voice messages play once for the recipient and the audio is deleted right after. Messages that are never played are deleted after 10 days.
We cannot stop someone from recording a message with another device while it plays. Do not send anything you would not want kept.

sections.heading: News and third-party links
body: Some topics are created automatically from public news feeds (RSS) of education news sites and of the universities themselves and contain only the headline and a link to the full article. Articles belong to their publishers.
We do not control or endorse third-party websites, or the opinions users express in their voices.

body: We grant you a personal, non-exclusive, non-transferable, revocable licence to use the app on Apple devices you own or control, as permitted by the App Store Usage Rules. Speak's name, design and code belong to us.
You may not copy, decompile or modify the app, scrape the service by automated means, or use it in a way that overloads it or harms others.

sections.heading: Deletion and termination

We may suspend or terminate your access if you break these terms or the law.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what personal data Speak processes when you use the iOS app or the website, why, on what legal basis, how long we keep it and what rights you have under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Speak is a voice social network, so your voice is the main data you share.

sections.heading: Controller and contact
body: The controller is {controller}, operator of the Speak service.
For anything about your data contact {email} or call {phone}. We reply within one month at the latest.

sections.heading: What data we collect
body: Account: email, full name and password, stored only in hashed form.
Profile: username (@username), name and profile photo (optional).

Student identity (optional): university, school and year of study. To confirm it we send a code to your university email; the email is not stored — we keep only an irreversible fingerprint (hash) so that each university email matches one account. You can remove it at any time in Settings.

Public voices: the recordings you post (up to 2 minutes), their title, section and topic, the time of posting, and your voice replies, reposts and quotes. Your voice is personal data because it can identify you and reveal information about you.
Activity: who you follow and who follows you, likes, which voices you have played (for the listen counter, once per voice), blocks, reports you make or that are made about you, in-app notifications.
Voice messages: the audio of each message is stored only until the recipient plays it, together with sender, recipient, time sent and whether it was played.

Walkie-talkie: when you hold the button and talk to a friend, your voice is streamed live only to them through Supabase Realtime (not stored there). Each transmission is also saved, with sender, recipient, length and time, so the two of you can replay it for 24 hours. Your friends' channels are always open while the app is open: they see you as "here" and you hear them live. A transmission you missed leaves a notification. If part of a transmission is lost live, the app plays the saved copy right after and records technical diagnostics (how many audio pieces were sent or arrived, connection and audio state, device/browser type — never audio), deleted after 3 days.
Technical data: IP address, device/browser type, server logs and a log of actions for usage limits (rate limits), needed to run and secure the service.

Microphone: used only while you record or hold the walkie-talkie button, after you grant permission. A recording stays on your device until you tap "Post" or "Send"; on the walkie-talkie your voice reaches your friend live while you talk.

Notifications: the daily topic reminders are scheduled locally on your device. If you allow notifications in the app, we keep your device's push identifier (APNs token) and the app language, to send you notifications through Apple about messages, replies, new files in the courses you take and so on. It is deleted when you sign out or delete your account; you can turn notifications off in the iPhone's Settings.
We do not collect location, contacts, payment or health data. We do not transcribe your voice, use it for biometric identification or use it to train artificial intelligence systems.
When you sign up with your student email, your university address is also your account email: you sign in with a one-time code we send you, no password.

Course files: the documents and photos you upload to a course, with their title, type (notes or past papers), size and time. We also record which classmates opened a file (once each) and who said «Thanks», the courses you mark «I'm taking it», and from these we compute points and the department's board. An uploader sees only how many downloaded their file, not who; those who said «Thanks» appear in their notifications.

sections.heading: Purposes and legal basis
body: Performance of a contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR): your account, posting and playing voices, followers, likes, replies, voice messages, notifications and account emails (sign-up confirmation, password reset).

Legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR): security, preventing spam and abuse, usage limits, handling reports and moderating content, ranking the "For you" feed using likes, replies, reposts, listens and who you follow.
Consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR): profile photo, microphone and notification permissions, which you can withdraw at any time in the app or in your device settings.
Legal obligation (Art. 6(1)(c) GDPR): when the law or a competent authority requires us to keep or disclose data.
We do not use your data for advertising, do not sell it and do not track you across other apps or websites. Feed ranking does not produce decisions with legal or similarly significant effects on you.

sections.heading: Who can see your data
body: Other users: your name, @username, photo, public voices (with title, time, likes, replies, reposts and listen count) and follower lists are visible to every signed-in user. Who played or liked a voice is not shown. Your email is never shown.
Your university, school and year (if you added them) are shown on your profile to every signed-in user.

Audio files of public voices are stored under a random, unguessable link: anyone who obtains a file's link can play it. Voice messages are not stored under such a link and only the recipient can play them, once. Walkie-talkie transmissions are not stored under such a link; only you and your friend can play them.
People you block cannot see your content or contact you.

Speak administrators: have access only as needed for support and for reviewing reports (e.g. playing a public voice that was reported). Voice messages are not available in the admin tools. The same goes for the walkie-talkie.

Post links: when someone shares a post's link, anyone who opens it (even without an account) sees only your first name, your university and department, the post's text and its numbers of likes and replies — not the voice, the photos, your surname or your profile photo. Group posts are never shown this way.
Files you upload to a course, with your name, are visible only to verified students of your university, through links that expire after one hour.

sections.heading: Location and map
body: Only if you turn it on (Profile → ⚙︎ → “Location”), the app sends your exact position (latitude/longitude, accuracy, heading, speed), also with the app closed if you allow “Always”. Legal basis: your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR), which you withdraw at any time by turning it off.

Who sees it: with “Friends only”, people you follow each other with; with “Everyone nearby”, also any user within 500 m of you who shares their location too, together with your name, @username and photo. The distance is measured from the other person's real position, not from a point they pick.

We keep only your latest position (no history), with its accuracy. Your friends see it with its time for up to 1 hour (like Find My); everyone else only if it is less than 15 minutes old. While you stand still the app re-sends it once a minute so it shows as current. It is deleted after 1 hour, immediately when you turn sharing off, and when you delete your account. People you have blocked don't see you.

Voice on the map: when you press to talk to someone near you, we notify them with your name, photo and distance. The audio plays live and is kept for 24 hours so only the two of you can replay it, then it is deleted. You choose who may talk to you (everyone, people you follow, nobody); we only record when and to whom you talked (for abuse limits).

sections.heading: Service providers (processors)
body: Supabase Inc.: database, user authentication and storage of audio files, photos and documents.
Cloudflare, Inc.: hosting and running the app, protection against attacks.
Email delivery provider: sending sign-up confirmation and password reset emails.
Apple: distributes the app through the App Store, but has no access to your Speak account data.

For news topics our server reads public RSS feeds of education news sites and universities; we do not send them any user data. News photos are shown straight from the publisher's server, so when you see them or open an article link, the publisher receives your IP address under its own policy.
All providers process data only on our instructions and are bound by data processing agreements (Art. 28 GDPR). Data may also be disclosed to public authorities when required by law.
OpenFreeMap: map images are loaded from its servers when you open the map (they see your device's IP address and the map area requested, not your account or your position).
Apple (Apple Push Notification service): delivers push notifications to your iPhone; it receives the device identifier and the notification text.

sections.heading: Transfers outside the EEA
body: Some providers are based in the US or may process data outside the European Economic Area. In those cases transfers rely on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework or the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses.

sections.heading: How long we keep data
body: Your account, profile and public voices are kept while your account is active or until you delete them. When you delete a voice, its audio file, title, likes, listens and plain reposts are deleted. If others had replied to it or quoted it, their voices stay and "This voice was deleted" is shown in its place, without a name or audio.

Voice messages: the audio is deleted as soon as it is played, or after 10 days if it is never played. Conversation records (who sent to whom and when), and the texts and photos you send in direct messages, are deleted after 90 days. Message photos are stored privately: only you and the recipient can see them.
Walkie-talkie: each transmission (audio and details) is deleted automatically after 24 hours, or at once if you block the other person.
Content reports are kept as long as needed for community safety and dealing with repeated violations. Server logs are kept for a limited time by the hosting providers.
Course files stay until you delete them or your account is deleted (or they are removed after a report).

sections.heading: Deleting your account
body: You can permanently delete your account in the app: Profile → ⚙︎ → "Delete account". Alternatively, send a request to {email}.

Deletion immediately removes your account, profile, photo, all your voices and their audio files, likes, followers, blocks, notifications, and the voice messages and walkie-talkie transmissions you sent or received. Voices of yours that others had replied to or quoted remain as "This voice was deleted" without a name, audio or title, so their voices are not lost. Reports you made remain without any link to you.

sections.heading: Your rights
body: You have the right of access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, data portability and to object to processing based on legitimate interest (Arts. 15–21 GDPR), and to withdraw consent at any time without affecting the lawfulness of earlier processing.
You can change your name, @username and photo in your profile and delete any voice from its ⋯ menu. For other requests email {email}. We may ask you to confirm your identity.
If you believe your rights are infringed, you can lodge a complaint with the Hellenic Data Protection Authority (1-3 Kifisias Ave., 115 23 Athens, www.dpa.gr).

sections.heading: Security
body: All communication is encrypted (HTTPS). Passwords are stored only in hashed form. Access to data is enforced at database level so every user sees only what they are entitled to, and admin keys live only on the server, never in the app.
No system is completely secure. If we detect a breach that puts you at risk, we will inform you and the Authority as the law requires.

sections.heading: Minors
body: The service is for people aged 15 and over (Art. 21 Law 4624/2019). If you are a parent and believe a child under 15 has created an account, contact us and we will delete it.

sections.heading: Cookies and local storage
body: We only use strictly necessary local storage on your device: to keep you signed in and to remember preferences such as language and the daily reminder.
We do not use advertising or analytics cookies and do not track you across apps and websites.

sections.heading: Changes to this policy
body: We may update this policy when the service or the law changes. The date of the last update is shown at the top. We will tell you about material changes in the app or by email.

metrics.readyNote: Readiness = O4 proposal (an indicator only, it opens nothing): ≥ 8 students, ≥ 3 active in 7 days, ≥ 3 course files or questions in 30 days. Material = files + questions of 30 days.
metrics.definitions: Active = did anything we record (post, reply, like, listen, download, upload, thanks, «take», group, message, follow). Contributor = posted / replied or uploaded in 30 days. Activation = students verified 7–90 days ago who, in their first week, posted, uploaded, thanked, took a course, joined a group they chose or messaged. Return = students verified 14–90 days ago who were active on days 7–14.
